ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Soil contains many kinds of living organisms. Bacteria and fungi help break down organic matter and cycle nutrients.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Mobung ho na le mefuta e mengata ya dintho tse phelang. Baktheria le fungi di thusa ho qhaqha organic matter le ho tsamaisa dimatlafatsi ka potoloho.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Some fungi help roots take up nutrients. Worm channels can help water and air enter soil.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Fungi tse ding di thusa metso ho monya dimatlafatsi. Meselana e entsweng ke diboko e ka thusa metsi le moya ho kena mobung.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Put soil and water in a clear jar, with a little suitable dispersing detergent. Close and shake it, then leave it undisturbed.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Kenya mobu le metsi ka clear jar, o kenye hanyenyane ya suitable dispersing detergent. E kwale mme o e sisinye, ebe o e siya e sa sisinyehe.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Sand settles first. Silt settles next, while clay can remain suspended much longer.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Sand e dula fatshe pele. Silt e latela, athe clay e ka nna ya dula e suspended nako e telele haholo.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: This is a rough learning exercise. Clumps and unsettled clay can mislead you; use a soil laboratory when accurate texture is needed.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Ena ke rough learning exercise feela. Dikgobokano tsa mobu (clumps) le clay e so duleng fatshe di ka o kgelosa; sebedisa soil laboratory ha o hloka soil texture e nepahetseng.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: A thick sand layer beneath cloudy water does not yet tell you the final proportions. Some fine particles may still be suspended.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Lera le letenya la sand ka tlasa cloudy water ha le eso o bolelle final proportions. Fine particles tse ding di ka nna tsa dula di suspended.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Compaction, poor drainage and loss of organic matter can limit roots and soil life.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Ho thatafala ha mobu (compaction), drainage e mpe le tahlehelo ya organic matter di ka sitisa metso le bophelo ba mobu.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Time to readiness varies with materials, moisture, air and temperature. A province name or a fixed number of weeks is not a readiness test.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Nako ya hore compost e lokele ho sebediswa e fapana ho ya ka materials, mongobo, moya le thempereitjha. Lebitso la province kapa palo e behilweng ya dibeke ha se readiness test.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Mix dry browns with fresh greens. Avoid thick, wet layers that keep air out.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Kopanya dry browns le fresh greens. Qoba layers tse teteaneng, tse metsi tse thibelang moya ho kena.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: If the heap becomes slimy or smells strongly of ammonia, add dry browns and turn it.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Ha qubu ya compost e ka ba slimy kapa e nkha ammonia haholo, eketsa dry browns mme o e phethole.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Check moisture and air as the heap changes; one recipe does not suit every mix of materials.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Hlahloba mongobo le moya ha qubu ya compost e ntse e fetoha; recipe e le nngwe ha e tshwanele motswako o mong le o mong wa materials.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: A hot centre does not prove that every part of a heap has been treated. Time, temperature and management all matter.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Karolo e bohareng e tjhesang ya qubu ha e pake hore karolo e nngwe le e nngwe ya yona e se e treated. Nako, temperature le management kaofela di bohlokwa.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste and contaminated materials out of this simple household system.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Boloka meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste le contaminated materials di le ka ntle ho tsamaiso ena e bonolo ya lapeng.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Do not assume home composting destroys every weed seed or disease organism. Use a recognised process where sanitation is required.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: U se ke ua nahana hore home composting e fedisa peo e nngwe le e nngwe ya mofoka kapa disease organism e nngwe le e nngwe. Sebedisa recognised process moo sanitation e hlokahalang.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep wattle seed pods out of the compost heap. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Boloka wattle seed pods di le ka ntle ho qubu ya compost. Qubu e tlwaelehileng e ka nna ya se etse hore peo e nngwe le e nngwe e be non-viable.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Use only clean, untreated materials. Bark breaks down slowly; its name alone is not proof that it is free of contamination.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Sebedisa materials tse hlwekileng feela, tse sa alafwang. Bark e bola butle; lebitso la yona feela ha le pake hore ha e na contamination.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Check the heap and turn when it needs more air or mixing. Keep it moist rather than waterlogged.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Hlahloba qubu ya compost mme o e phethole ha e hloka moya o mongata kapa ho kopanngwa. E boloke e le mongobo, e se ke ya ba waterlogged.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Cover bare soil with suitable clean mulch, such as straw, dry grass or wood chips.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Koahela mobu o pepesitsweng ka mulch e hlwekileng e loketseng, jwalo ka straw, dry grass kapa wood chips.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Check moisture underneath and adjust the layer; more mulch is not always better.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: E boloke e le hole le trunks and stems. Hlahloba mongobo ka tlasa mulch mme o fetole layer ha ho hlokahala; mulch e ngata ha e dule e le betere.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Cover crops can protect ground between main crops. Choose for local weather, available water and the next planting.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Cover crops di ka sireletsa mobu pakeng tsa main crops. Di kgethe ho latela boemo ba lehodimo ba sebakeng sa heno, metsi a fumanehang le next planting.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Legumes need suitable bacteria and growing conditions to fix nitrogen. Nutrients in their residues become available as the material decomposes.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Legumes di hloka bacteria tse loketseng le maemo a kgolo a loketseng hore di kgone ho fix nitrogen. Dimatlafatsi tse masalleng a tsona di a fumaneha ha thepa eo e ntse e bola.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Worm farms can turn suitable food scraps and bedding into castings. Check the bin rather than expecting a fixed harvest date.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Worm farms di ka fetola food scraps le bedding tse loketseng hore e be worm castings. Hlahloba bin ho e-na le ho lebella letsatsi le behilweng la kotulo.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin is called leachate. It is not the same as a prepared worm-casting tea.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin e bitswa leachate. Ha o tshwane le worm-casting tea e lokisitsweng.
englishClauses: liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Leachate can contain harmful organisms or substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Leachate e ka ba le harmful organisms kapa substances. O se ke wa e sebedisa hodima edible plants kapa wa nahana hore ho e hlapolla ho etsa hore e bolokehe.

ordinaryWordsRetained.english: Keep Seed Pods and Contaminants Out
ordinaryWordsRetained.text: Siyani Zwikhwama zwa Mbeu na Contaminants Nnḓa
ordinaryWordsRetained.why: 'Contaminants' kept in English as the Tshivenda Soil lesson keeps this idea in English ('Siyani seed pods na contaminated materials nnḓa ha heap'). The earlier draft word 'zwiṱhaphudzi' occurs nowhere in the course and a blind reader could not resolve it. Seed pods are now 'zwikhwama zwa mbeu', the manual's phrase, replacing 'zwikhopha', which means aloes.

ordinaryWordsRetained.english: If your compost smells of ammonia and feels slimy, add dry carbon such as straw and turn it.
ordinaryWordsRetained.text: Arali compost yaṋu i tshi nukha ammonia nahone ni tshi i fara ya vha slimy, shelani carbon yo omaho u fana na straw nahone ni i rembuluse.
ordinaryWordsRetained.why: 'slimy' and 'straw' kept in English as the current Tshivenda learner wording keeps them (learner s11.p1 'ya vha slimy'; learner mulch text 'straw'). Native candidates failed two blind back-translation rounds ('tshetemudza' read as wet/sticky; 'mahatsi' read as grass, which would invert the dry-carbon instruction).

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Soil contains many kinds of living organisms. Bacteria and fungi help break down organic matter and cycle nutrients.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Mavu a na mifuda minzhi ya living organisms. Bacteria na fungi dzi thusa u kwashekanya organic matter na u cycle nutrients.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Some fungi help roots take up nutrients. Worm channels can help water and air enter soil.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Dziṅwe fungi dzi thusa midzi u dzhia nutrients. Worm channels dzi nga thusa uri maḓi na muya zwi dzhene mavuni.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Put soil and water in a clear jar, with a little suitable dispersing detergent. Close and shake it, then leave it undisturbed.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Vheani soil na water kha clear jar, ni engedze little suitable dispersing detergent. Ni vale jar, ni i dzinginye, ni i sie i sa tshintshwi.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Sand settles first. Silt settles next, while clay can remain suspended much longer.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Sand i settles pele. Silt i settles nga murahu, ngeno clay i tshi nga sala i suspended much longer.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: This is a rough learning exercise. Clumps and unsettled clay can mislead you; use a soil laboratory when accurate texture is needed.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Hezwi ndi rough learning exercise. Clumps na clay i sa athu settled zwi nga ni xedza; shumisani soil laboratory musi accurate texture i tshi ṱoḓea.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: A thick sand layer beneath cloudy water does not yet tell you the final proportions. Some fine particles may still be suspended.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Thick sand layer nga fhasi ha cloudy water a i athu u ni vhudza final proportions. Fine particles dzi nga kha ḓi vha suspended.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Record what you see and what remains uncertain. Do not prescribe watering or soil treatments from one jar alone.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Ṅwalani zwe na zwi vhona na zwine zwa kha ḓi sa vha khagala. Ni songo dzhia phetho ya u sheledza kana u lafha mavu nga u sedza jar nthihi fhedzi.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Compaction, poor drainage and loss of organic matter can limit roots and soil life.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Compaction, poor drainage na loss ya organic matter zwi nga limit midzi na soil life.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Pale colour or few worms do not prove that chemicals killed the soil. Worm activity also changes with moisture and season.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Pale colour kana few worms a zwi prove uri chemicals dzo vhulaha mavu. U shuma ha worms na hone hu a shanduka u ya nga moisture na season.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Look for patterns across the field. Check management history, drainage and plant growth before choosing a remedy.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Sedzani patterns tsimuni. Sedzani management history, drainage na u aluwa ha plants ni sa athu khetha remedy.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Compost is organic matter broken down under managed conditions.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Compost ndi organic matter yo broken down nga fhasi ha managed conditions.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Finished compost can improve soil structure and contribute nutrients.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Compost yo fhelelaho i nga khwinifhadza tshivhumbeo tsha mavu, na u contribute nutrients.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Mix dry browns with fresh greens. Avoid thick, wet layers that keep air out.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Tanganyani dry browns na fresh greens. Avoid thick, wet layers that keep air out.
englishClauses: wet layers that keep air out

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: If the heap becomes slimy or smells strongly of ammonia, add dry browns and turn it.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Arali thulwi ya manyoro ya vha slimy kana ya nukha ammonia nga maanḓa, shelani dry browns nahone ni i rembuluse.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Check moisture and air as the heap changes; one recipe does not suit every mix of materials.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Sedzulusani vhunyunyu na muya musi thulwi i tshi khou shanduka; recipe nthihi a i lulameli mutanganyo muṅwe na muṅwe wa materials.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: A hot centre does not prove that every part of a heap has been treated. Time, temperature and management all matter.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Hot centre a i khwaṱhisedzi uri tshipida tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe tsha thulwi tsho treated. Time, temperature na management zwoṱhe zwi na ndeme.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste and contaminated materials out of this simple household system.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Iledzani u dzhenisa nyama, dairy, zwimela zwi re na malwadze, pet waste na contaminated materials kha iyi simple household system.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Do not assume home composting destroys every weed seed or disease organism. Use a recognised process where sanitation is required.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Ni songo humbula uri home composting i fhedza weed seed iṅwe na iṅwe kana disease organism iṅwe na iṅwe. Shumisani recognised process hune sanitation ya ṱoḓea.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep wattle seed pods out of the compost heap. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Iledzani u dzhenisa wattle seed pods kha thulwi ya manyoro. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.
englishClauses: an ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Use only clean, untreated materials. Bark breaks down slowly; its name alone is not proof that it is free of contamination.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Shumisani fhedzi clean, untreated materials. Bark breaks down slowly; dzina layo fhedzi a si proof ya uri a i na contamination.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Check the heap and turn when it needs more air or mixing. Keep it moist rather than waterlogged.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Sedzulusani thulwi ni i rembuluse musi i tshi toda muya wo engedzeaho kana u tanganiswa. Keep it moist, hu si waterlogged.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Cover bare soil with suitable clean mulch, such as straw, dry grass or wood chips.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Fukedzani mavu a songo fukwaho nga mulch yo kunaho, yo teaho, u fana na straw, hatsi ho omaho kana wood chips.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Check moisture underneath and adjust the layer; more mulch is not always better.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Sedzani moisture nga fhasi hayo ni lulamise layer; mulch nnzhi a i dzuli i tshi vha yavhuḓi.
englishClauses: keep it clear of trunks and stems

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Cover crops can protect ground between main crops. Choose for local weather, available water and the next planting.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Cover crops dzi nga tsireledza mavu vhukati ha main crops. Khethani u ya nga mutsho wa henefho, maḓi ane a vha hone na next planting.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: The course examples include oats, lupins, sunn hemp and cowpea. Check local suitability before sowing.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Tsumbo dza course dzi katela oats, lupins, sunn hemp na cowpea. Sedzani arali dzi tshi fanela fhethu haṋu ni sa athu dzi zwala.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Legumes need suitable bacteria and growing conditions to fix nitrogen. Nutrients in their residues become available as the material decomposes.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Legumes dzi ṱoḓa bacteria dzo teaho na growth conditions dzo teaho u fix nitrogen. Nutrients dzi re kha masalela adzo dzi a wanala musi material i tshi decompose.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Worm farms can turn suitable food scraps and bedding into castings. Check the bin rather than expecting a fixed harvest date.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Worm farms dzi nga shandula food scraps na bedding zwo teaho zwa vha castings. Sedzani bin, ni songo lavhelela fixed harvest date.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin is called leachate. It is not the same as a prepared worm-casting tea.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin i vhidzwa leachate. A si tshithu tshithihi na prepared worm-casting tea.
englishClauses: liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Leachate can contain harmful organisms or substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Leachate i nga vha na harmful organisms kana substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.
englishClauses: do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: The first heavy spring storm can strike bare ground and damage its surface and structure. If water runs over the field, it can carry loosened soil away.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Storm ya u thoma khulwane ya spring i nga rwa mavu a songo fukedzwaho, ya tshinyadza surface na structure ya hone. Arali maḓi a tshi elela nṱha ha field, a nga hwala loosened soil a a bvisa.

ordinaryWordsRetained.english: Keep Seed Pods and Contaminants Out
ordinaryWordsRetained.text: Seed Pods ni Swithyakisi: Swi Tshike Ehandle
ordinaryWordsRetained.why: No confirmed Xitsonga word for 'seed pods': 'swikhwama' reads as bags and 'xikhumba' also means bark (s13.p1). Kept in English for facilitator review; the learner paragraph s13.p0 also keeps 'wattle seed pods' in English.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Soil contains many kinds of living organisms. Bacteria and fungi help break down organic matter and cycle nutrients.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Misava yi na tinxaka to tala ta swilo leswi hanyaka. Bacteria na fungi swi pfuna ku fayelela organic matter ni ku cycle nutrients.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Some fungi help roots take up nutrients. Worm channels can help water and air enter soil.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Fungi tin'wana ti pfuna timitsu ku tswonga nutrients. Worm channels ti nga pfuna mati na moya ku nghena emhlabeni.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Put soil and water in a clear jar, with a little suitable dispersing detergent. Close and shake it, then leave it undisturbed.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Chela misava na mati eka clear jar, u chela nyana suitable dispersing detergent. Pfala jar u yi ninginika, kutani u yi tshika yi nga ninginiki.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Sand settles first. Silt settles next, while clay can remain suspended much longer.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Sand yi sungula ku tshamisa ehansi. Silt yi tshamisa endzhaku ka yona, kasi clay yi nga ha sala yi suspended much longer.

ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Lowu i rough learning exercise. Clumps na clay leyi nga si tshamaka ehansi swi nga ku hambukisa; tirhisa soil laboratory loko ku laveka accurate soil texture.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: A thick sand layer beneath cloudy water does not yet tell you the final proportions. Some fine particles may still be suspended.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Thick sand layer ehansi ka cloudy water a yi si komba final proportions. Fine particles tin’wana ti nga ha va suspended.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Record what you see and what remains uncertain. Do not prescribe watering or soil treatments from one jar alone.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Tsala leswi u swi vonaka ni leswi nga si tiyiseka. U nga teki xiboho xa ku cheleta kumbe ku tirhisa ndlela yo lulamisa misava hi ku ya hi jar yin’we ntsena.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Compaction, poor drainage and loss of organic matter can limit roots and soil life.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Compaction, poor drainage na ku lahleka ka organic matter can limit timitsu ni soil life.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Pale colour or few worms do not prove that chemicals killed the soil. Worm activity also changes with moisture and season.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Muhlovo lowu nga vonakaka wa pale kumbe few worms a swi tiyisisi leswaku chemicals ti dlayile misava. Worm activity na yona ya cinca hi ku ya hi moisture na season.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Look for patterns across the field. Check management history, drainage and plant growth before choosing a remedy.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Languta patterns leti humelelaka ensin'wini hinkwaro. Kambela management history, drainage ni ku kula ka swimilani u nga si hlawula remedy.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Compost is organic matter broken down under managed conditions.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Compost i organic matter leyi broken down ehansi ka managed conditions.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Finished compost can improve soil structure and contribute nutrients.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Finished compost yi nga antswisa xivumbeko xa misava ni ku contribute nutrients.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Time to readiness varies with materials, moisture, air and temperature. A province name or a fixed number of weeks is not a readiness test.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Nkarhi wo lungheka wa hambana hi materials, moisture, air na temperature. Vito ra province kumbe nhlayo leyi vekiweke ya mavhiki a hi readiness test.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Mix dry browns with fresh greens. Avoid thick, wet layers that keep air out.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Hlanganisa dry browns na fresh greens. Papalata thick, wet layers leti sivelaka air ku nghena.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: If the heap becomes slimy or smells strongly of ammonia, add dry browns and turn it.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Check moisture and air as the heap changes; one recipe does not suit every mix of materials.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Kambela moisture na air loko heap yi ri karhi yi cinca; recipe yin'we a yi ringani eka nkatsakanyo wun'wana ni wun'wana wa materials.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: A hot centre does not prove that every part of a heap has been treated. Time, temperature and management all matter.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Hot centre ya heap a yi tiyisisi leswaku every part ya heap yi treated. Time, temperature and management all matter.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste and contaminated materials out of this simple household system.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Hlayisani meat, dairy, diseased plants, pet waste na contaminated materials swi ri ehandle ka simple household system.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Do not assume home composting destroys every weed seed or disease organism. Use a recognised process where sanitation is required.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: U nga teki leswaku home composting yi lovisa weed seed yin'wana ni yin'wana kumbe disease organism yin'wana ni yin'wana. Tirhisa recognised process laha sanitation yi lavekaka.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep wattle seed pods out of the compost heap. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Hlayisani wattle seed pods ehandle ka compost heap. An ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable.
englishClauses: an ordinary heap may not make every seed non-viable

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Use only clean, untreated materials. Bark breaks down slowly; its name alone is not proof that it is free of contamination.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Tirhisa clean, untreated materials ntsena. Bark breaks down slowly; vito ra yona ntsena a hi vumbhoni bya leswaku a yi na contamination.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Check the heap and turn when it needs more air or mixing. Keep it moist rather than waterlogged.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Kambela heap kutani u yi turn loko yi lava air yo tala kumbe mixing. Yi hlayise yi ri moist, ku nga ri waterlogged.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Cover bare soil with suitable clean mulch, such as straw, dry grass or wood chips.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Funengetani misava leyi nga hava cover hi mulch leyi basekile, leyi faneleke, yo fana na straw, byanyi byo oma kumbe wood chips.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Check moisture underneath and adjust the layer; more mulch is not always better.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Keep it clear of trunks and stems. Kambelani moisture ehansi ka yona, mi lulamisa layer; mulch yo tala a yi vuli leswaku swi ta antswa nkarhi wun'wana ni wun'wana.
englishClauses: keep it clear of trunks and stems

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Cover crops can protect ground between main crops. Choose for local weather, available water and the next planting.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Cover crops ti nga sirhelela misava leyi nga kona between main crops. Ti hlawuleni hi ku ya hi weather ya laha, mati lama kumekaka ni next planting.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: The course examples include oats, lupins, sunn hemp and cowpea. Check local suitability before sowing.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Swikombiso swa course swi katsa oats, lupins, sunn hemp na cowpea. Kambelani loko swi fanele ndhawu ya kwalaho mi nga si swi byala.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Legumes need suitable bacteria and growing conditions to fix nitrogen. Nutrients in their residues become available as the material decomposes.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Legumes ti lava bacteria leti faneleke ni suitable growing conditions leswaku ti fix nitrogen. Nutrients leti nga eka masalela ya tona ta kumeka loko material yi ri karhi yi bola.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Worm farms can turn suitable food scraps and bedding into castings. Check the bin rather than expecting a fixed harvest date.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Worm farms ti nga hundzuluxa food scraps ni bedding leswi faneleke swi va castings. Kambelani bin ematshan'weni yo langutela fixed harvest date.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin is called leachate. It is not the same as a prepared worm-casting tea.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin yi vuriwa leachate. A yi fani na prepared worm-casting tea.
englishClauses: liquid that drains naturally from a worm bin

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Leachate can contain harmful organisms or substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Leachate yi nga va na harmful organisms kumbe substances. Do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe.
englishClauses: do not use it on edible plants or assume that dilution makes it safe

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Pula e matla e ka tlatsa swale ka potlako ho feta kamoo metsi a kenellang mobung. Rera safe overflow pele o tjheka.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Route eo ha e a tshwanela ho senya slope ka erosion kapa ho romela metsi a senyang ho moahisani. Downstream swale kapa dam e lokela ho kgona ho amohela metsi ao ka polokeho.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Kopa trained local adviser hore a hlahlobe mobu, slope le storm flow. Setshwantsho ha se construction design.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Slope feela ha e bolele hore swale e a lokela. Soil, drainage, unstable ground le metsi a tswang upslope kaofela di bohlokwa.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Boloka ground cover e ntle. Fumana local assessment pele o tjheka mobung o steep, wet kapa unstable. Grass barriers le terraces le tsona di hloka design e loketseng site.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Dihla tsa pula di fapana ho pholletsa le Afrika Borwa (South Africa). Sebedisa ditlaleho tsa sebaka seo mme o rale bakeng sa dry periods; letamo le tletseng ha le a tiisetswa.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Metsi a ka lahleha ka evaporation and seepage. Hlahloba boemo ba metsi mme o batle dibaka tse dutlang kapa kgoholeho.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. O se ke wa jala difate hodima lerako la letamo la mobu.
englishClauses: clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Bapisa phepelo le tshebediso eo o e rerileng.
englishClauses: an annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Bongata bo hlokahalang ba ho kgeloha bo itshetlehile ka marulelo le tsamaiso. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.
englishClauses: there is no single volume for every roof
use the suppliers sizing and maintenance instructions

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Boholo ba tanka bo itshetlehile ka tlhoko ya metsi, pula, boholo ba marulelo le the length of dry periods.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Boloka tanka e kwahetswe, screen openings against insects, mme o hlokomele marulelo, dikoto le sekgelo (diverter). Boloka metsi a pula a arohane le diphaephe tsa metsi a nowang.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Botsa balaodi ba bophelo bo botle ba sebaka seo ka diteko le kalafo tse loketseng tshebediso e rerilweng.
englishClauses: water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Haeba reuse system e se e sebetsa and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, emisa ho e sebedisa mme seek qualified local advice.

wholeUnitEnglish.english: If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Pula khulwane i nga ḓadza swale nga u ṱavhanya u fhira u dzhena ha maḓi mavuni. Plan a safe overflow before digging.
englishClauses: plan a safe overflow before digging

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Route a i tei u erode slope kana u rumela damaging water kha neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.
englishClauses: or dam must be able to receive it safely

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. Tshifanyiso a si construction design.
englishClauses: ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Slope fhedzi a i sumbedzi arali swale i suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground na maḓi ane a bva upslope zwoṱhe zwi na ndeme.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Keep good ground cover. Wanani local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers na terraces na zwone zwi ṱoḓa a design suited to the site.
englishClauses: a design suited to the site
local assessment before digging on steep

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Dam kana pond i nga vhulunga runoff, fhedzi amount i re hone i bva kha local rain, catchment, losses na uri ni shumisa maḓi mangana.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Tshifhinga tsha mvula tshi a fhambana u mona na Afurika Tshipembe. Shumisani local records ni pulanele dry periods; dam yo ḓalaho a yo khwaṱhisedzwi.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Musi ni sa athu shandula watercourse kana u fhaṱa storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.
englishClauses: check the required authorisation with the water authority

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Dam i ṱoḓa site investigation na design yo itwaho nga suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk na safe spillway zwoṱhe zwi na ndeme.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Do not assume that annual rainfall tells you the size of a flood or the storage you will have.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Ni songo humbula uri annual rainfall i ni vhudza size ya flood kana storage ine na ḓo vha nayo.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Overflow i songo langiwaho i nga erode na breach wall. Plan safe route ya excess water before construction.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Maḓi a nga xela nga evaporation na seepage. Check water level ni sedze leaks kana erosion.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Keep spillway i clear nahone maintain bank cover yo bulwaho kha design. Do not plant trees on earth dam wall.
englishClauses: do not plant trees on earth dam wall

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. U vha hone hazwi iti uri maḓi a vhe clean kana safe.
englishClauses: animals can damage banks and add manure to the water

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Ṱolani arali roof material yo tea u kuvhanganya maḓi a mvula musi ni sa athu u ṱumanya tank.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Shumisani roof area ine ya vhonala u bva nṱha na local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.
englishClauses: is diverted or overflows a full tank
then allow for water that misses the gutter

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Tshivhalo tsha ṅwaha woṱhe a tshi ni vhudzi uri hu ḓo vha na madi mangana during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.
englishClauses: compare supply with the uses you plan

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Roof runoff i nga hwala buse, droppings na iṅwe contamination. First-flush diverter i thivhela maṅwe maḓi a first runoff uri a si dzhene kha tank.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Diversion ine ya ṱoḓea i ḓitika nga ṱhanga na system. Shumisani ndaela dza supplier dza sizing na maintenance; a hu na volume nthihi fhedzi ine ya shuma kha ṱhanga iṅwe na iṅwe.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Tank size i ḓitika nga water demand, mvula, roof area na vhulapfu ha tshifhinga tsha dry periods.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Ṅwalani mutevhe wa intended uses nahone ni anganyele demand yayo u bva kha records dzaṋu vhaṋe. Compare that with supply through the seasons.
englishClauses: compare that with supply through the seasons

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Pulannani zwine na ḓo zwi ita musi maḓi o vhulungwaho a tshi thoma u vha maṱuku. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.
englishClauses: a province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Itani uri tank i dzule yo tibifhiwa; screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.
englishClauses: keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Vhudzisani local health authority nga ha testing na treatment yo teelaho intended use.
englishClauses: water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Basic filter fhedzi a si drinking-water guarantee. Maḓi ane a shumiswa kha food crops na one a ṱoḓa safety assessment.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Hlayisa misava yi funengetekile kahle. Kuma nkambelo wa laha kaya u nga si cela eka steep, wet or unstable land. Mindzilakano ya byanyi (grass barriers) na titerasi (terraces) na swona swi lava dizayini leyi faneleke ndhawu.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Tinguva ta mpfula ti hambana eAfrika Dzonga hinkwayo. Tirhisa tirhekhodo ta le kusuhi naswona plan for dry periods; damu leri teleke a ri tiyisiwangi.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Loko u nga si cinca watercourse kumbe ku aka storage works, kamba authorisation leyi lavekaka eka water authority.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Damu ri lava site investigation na design hi munhu loyi a nga na suitable qualifications. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk na safe spillway, hinkwato i swa nkoka.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Kunguhatela ndlela leyi hlayisekeke ya mati lama taleke ngopfu u nga si sungula ku aka.
englishClauses: an uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Mati ma nga lahleka hi evaporation and seepage. Kamba xiyimo xa mati naswona u lavisisa ku lutla kumbe ku gogodeka ka misava.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Ku va kona ka swona a swi endli mati ma basa kumbe ku hlayiseka.
englishClauses: animals can damage banks and add manure to the water

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Tirhisa vukulu bya lwangu loko ri langutiwa hi le henhla na tirhekhodo ta mpfula ya le kusuhi. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.
englishClauses: is diverted or overflows a full tank
then allow for water that misses the gutter

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. First-flush diverter yi endla leswaku some of the first runoff yi nga ngheni etankini.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Sayizi ya thanki yi titshege hi xilaveko xa mati, mpfula, vukulu bya lwangu na vulehi bya dry periods.

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Tsala intended uses kutani u estimate demand ya wona u tirhisa tirhekhodo ta wena n'wini. Compare that with supply through the seasons.
englishClauses: compare that with supply through the seasons

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Kunguhatela leswi u nga ta swi endla loko mati lama hlayisiweke ma sungula ku va matsongo. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.
englishClauses: a province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Hlayisa thanki yi funengetiwile. Screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.
englishClauses: keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes

ordinaryEnglishInside.english: A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.
ordinaryEnglishInside.text: Basic filter ntsena a yi tiyisisi leswaku mati ma hlayisekile ku nwa. Mati lawa ya tirhisiwaka eka food crops na wona ya lava safety assessment.
